That completes every area you asked me to explore. Here's the **full picture** of what's settled and ready to build — all confirmed hands-on by you:

**Capturing & editing**
1. Quick save with page details filled in automatically; saves even when a page can't be read.
2. No duplicates — re-saving a link takes you to the existing one.
3. Edit title, address, description; odd input politely refused.

**Organising**
4. Tags — several per bookmark, with reuse suggestions.
5. Tag filter — three-state per tag (include / exclude / off), matching all includes and no excludes.
6. Personal notes in simple Markdown, separate from the page's own description.

**Finding**
7. Everyday search across everything, with highlighting.
8. Advanced query language — `#tag`, `"phrases"`, `AND/OR/NOT`, parentheses, safe fallback.
9. Saved named views — a search + include/exclude tag combination, reusable and persistent.

**Working through & tidying**
10. Read tracking — To read / Read, its own status, with focus views.
11. Archive (reversible) vs Delete (permanent, confirmed).
12. Select many — or all matching — and tag / mark / archive / delete them together.

**Keeping & moving**
13. Optional per-bookmark offline copy (single-file page snapshot, or the PDF itself) plus independent Internet Archive preservation.
14. Import & export standard browser bookmark files — folders become tags, existing links skipped.

**Throughout**
15. Sort (incl. recently-updated), how many to show, adjustable text size, saved as your default.
16. Comfortable on phone and desktop; long content wraps; robust empty/error states.

Deferred to a later round (you agreed): the automatic by-website view.

That's **18 settled behaviours**, with their boundary and error situations explored. **May I now switch from exploring to actually building this scope for real?**
